description.narrative: The intention of the ERI project is to expand the reach of legitimate government authority by working with FGS, FMSs and local communities. ERI will enable the FGS Ministry of Interior, Federal Affairs and Reconciliation (MoIFAR), FMSs Ministries of Interior, Local Governance and Reconciliation (MoILGR) and other partners and donors to engage in areas newly recovered from AS control (newly recovered areas, NRAs). ERI is part of a broader CSSF stabilisation programme that delivers a set of upstream interventions with both local and international actors to enhance civil-military coordination and influence Somalia’s overall approach to immediate and early recovery.

target.value: Wanlawyn CAP 5: 33 participants including 43% female Baidoa CAP 5: 33 participants including 43% female

actual.value:
Wanlaweyn district: 60 participants placed a spotlight on critical issues such as civilian protection, human rights, and crime prevention. Notably, seven of the participants were women, a deliberate effort by the ERI project to bridge the gender gap in the representation of women within security forces.. The decision to actively include women in this engagement is rooted in the understanding that women are often underrepresented in security forces and decision-making processes related to security.
Baidoa: a diverse cohort of 70 participants, including esteemed traditional elders, (25) women, and youth.
